title: Path to Digital Sustainability: The Value of Open Government Data in Corporate Carbon Emissions
affiliations: Renmin University of China, Shanghai University of International Business and Economics, University of Washington - Michael G. Foster School of Business and Tongji University - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Path to Digital Sustainability: The Value of Open Government Data in Corporate Carbon Emissions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: National Natural Science Foundation of China

detail.abstract: How to effectively reduce carbon emissions is critical to tackle the grand challenge of climate change. Prior mainstream information systems literature approaches environmental sustainability either through an energy-saving view of green IT or a sustainability-oriented system design lens of green IS. This study pivots to a novel data-centric paradigm. Given government as the largest owner of public administration data, we investigate whether and how open government data (OGD)—a non-coercive, boundary-spanning resource-influences corporate carbon emissions. Leveraging the progressive rollout of OGD platforms across cities as a quasi-natural experiment, we construct a large firm-year panel dataset and utilize the staggered difference-indifferences estimator to identify the effects. We find that the exogenous shock of a local OGD platform launch contributes to a 6.6% average reduction in corporate carbon emissions. To unpack the underlying mechanism of this digital sustainability, we provide empirical evidence that aligns with three potential pathways. The emission-reducing effect is amplified in regions with higher environmental attentiveness (suggesting an enhanced public monitoring effect of OGD), is greater for capital-restricted firms (revealing OGD's effect in alleviating financial constraints), and is stronger among firms possessing a pre-existing technological foundation (implying OGD's potential in facilitating active green innovation). Furthermore, platform design heterogeneity reveals that information richness, quality, and usage magnify the effects. This study extends the emerging literature on digital-enabled environmental sustainability beyond internal proprietary systems to the externality of open data sharing, demonstrating how OGD changes the information environment to discipline corporate emissions.

title: Governing Delegated Work with Generative Artificial Intelligence: Progress-Signal Reliability and Artifact-Based Verification
affiliations: Korea University Business School

detail.title: Governing Delegated Work with Generative Artificial Intelligence: Progress-Signal Reliability and Artifact-Based Verification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author confirms no conflicts of interest with any others
declarations.funderStatement: The author acknowledges no funding of this study.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for complex professional assignments that extend over many hours or days. During these assignments, users often receive progress updates before they can inspect the underlying work. This creates an underexamined governance risk, because an AI system may report that work is nearly complete even when little usable output exists. We examine this problem in a major manuscript revision delegated over a roughly three-day interaction window. In a diagnostic case, two AI configurations repeatedly reported 80-90% completion but delivered only skeletal documents. We define this gap, in which reported progress exceeds the inspectable work available at the time of the report, as communication-execution misalignment (CEM). A comparative pilot, a measurement audit, used nine AI-generated deliverables and five blind evaluators to ask whether a global human completeness score could provide a stable substitute for the system report. Under the initial rubric, evaluator judgments varied substantially, and the two quantities were not interchangeable. The study extends AI governance beyond final-output accuracy to the evidentiary reliability of interim work-state signals. It develops claim-evidence independence as a governance principle and artifact-based verification as its operational form, linking progress claims to inspectable, requirement-level evidence before additional work is delegated.

detail.abstract:
AI agents can translate a request into data access, system changes and delegated work. Control of the model's hosting environment does not establish control of these actions. The Sovereign AI Orchestration Control Framework (SAOCF) proposes an operating architecture through which an accountable organisation can define, enforce, observe and withdraw the authority delegated to an AI system.

SAOCF connects an authority envelope, six sovereignty invariants, seven control domains and 35 core controls. A six-dimensional Action Risk Vector informs A0-A5 authority classes. A nine-step execution loop binds policy and human approval to the actual operation, checks resource state and cumulative budgets, and reconciles downstream outcomes. Independently administered containment and protected evidence complete the control relationship.

The paper's contribution is an integrated specification linking organisational decision rights to resource-level enforcement and testable evidence. It draws on established AI risk management, zero trust, identity and incident response practice. It is intended for enterprise and public-sector executives, governance leaders, security architects, platform teams and assurance professionals designing bounded agent deployments.

title: Who Uses Platform AI First? Routine Currency under Common Technical Eligibility
affiliations: Korea University Business School

detail.title: Who Uses Platform AI First? Routine Currency under Common Technical Eligibility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author confirms no conflicts of interest with any others

detail.abstract: Platforms can make artificial intelligence (AI) services that automate recurring operating decisions available to all eligible sellers at once. Common eligibility, however, does not produce common use and leaves open who moves first once technical eligibility is shared. We examine recorded first use of a delegation-capable AI advertising service over 16 weeks among 69,288 platform-designated eligible sellers on a large e-commerce platform, estimating a discrete-time hazard model among 64,702 prior focal-platform advertisers. Among them, sellers whose routine had become dormant used the AI service far less often than those still advertising (0.43% versus 5.63%). Among active sellers, deeper resource commitment, expanding budgets, and more recent activity predicted earlier entry. These launch-proximate signals predicted first use better than longer advertising history. The commitment association is larger for the AI service than for three long-available non-AI advertising products. Platforms could stratify randomized onboarding experiments by whether related routines remain current.

title: The Timing of Privacy-Disclosure Reconfiguration: Concentration around Digital Product Releases
affiliations: Korea University Business School

detail.title: The Timing of Privacy-Disclosure Reconfiguration: Concentration around Digital Product Releases

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author confirms no conflicts of interest with any others
declarations.funderStatement: The author acknowledges no funding of this study.

detail.abstract: Digital products evolve through recurrent post-launch releases, whereas the standardized privacy disclosures attached to them are revised only rarely. Rarity of revision does not settle whether those rare revisions are timed independently of product evolution. We distinguish three temporal properties: event frequency (how often each process produces events), alignment (whether the events of one process fall near the other's recurring episodes), and sequence (whether one reliably precedes the other), and show that they can separate. Using a panel collected on a near-daily schedule from apps listed in the China App Store, we identify observationally persistent privacy-disclosure reconfigurations from disclosure data alone, reconstruct each app's release history independently, freeze the event set before introducing release information, and only then compare realized event dates with alternative observed dates in the same apps. Among the 31 events with reconstructed release support, 83.9% fall within seven days of a release, against an exact same-app null of 35.3%. The concentration survives local observed-date, temporalsupport, strict-reconstruction, calendar-dependence, and event-definition checks. The underlying revisions are interval-censored, so we identify unusual proximity rather than fixed ordering: the pattern is inconsistent with a fixed release-then-revision sequence while leaving exact ordering unresolved for most events. The findings show that administrative separability and low revision frequency do not imply temporal independence: rare revisions of a governance-facing representation can remain disproportionately aligned with a more frequent process of digital-product evolution without a fixed release-then-revision sequence.

title: Economic Incentives for Collective Restraint in Frontier AI Development Theory and quantitative scenarios using public spending and hardware evidence

detail.title: Economic Incentives for Collective Restraint in Frontier AI Development Theory and quantitative scenarios using public spending and hardware evidence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: There is no funding

detail.abstract: Frontier artificial intelligence laboratories may prefer collective restraint while continuing to accelerate individually. This paper examines that divergence through an innovation contest and a quantitative scenario analysis using public spending disclosures, hardware specifications, and supplier prices. The model separates returns to innovation from competition for relative advantage and establishes conditions under which a common reduction in development intensity increases incumbent profit. The financial analysis distinguishes allocated training cost, avoidable cash expenditure, and the value of deferring an investment. Repricing a disclosed training workload at assumed hourly rates gives a rental-equivalent cost of approximately US$60-190 million. For a hypothetical US$15 billion annual training budget, removing one quarter of planned activity saves approximately US$1.9 billion if half its associated expenditure is avoidable. At an assumed 60% contribution margin, the saving offsets approximately US$3.1 billion of annual incremental revenue forgone. An extension shows how incomplete collective restraint can eliminate that benefit: in the central example, coordination must remove at least 62.5% of the additional revenue penalty associated with slowing alone. These are conditional analytical results, not estimates of a named laboratory's savings or executives' motives. The strongest private incentive concerns future commitments and modest incremental commercial returns. The results identify expenditure flexibility and competitive displacement as central empirical variables, while leaving the socially desirable pace of innovation unresolved.

title: First Use Is Not Persistence: Platform AI Use in E-Commerce Marketplaces
affiliations: Korea University Business School

detail.title: First Use Is Not Persistence: Platform AI Use in E-Commerce Marketplaces

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author confirms no conflicts of interest with any others

detail.abstract: Seller-facing artificial intelligence (AI) tools are spreading rapidly across e-commerce platforms, and counting the sellers who first use them offers an easy, visible measure of rollout progress. Yet a first use shows only that a seller has entered, not whether the platform continues to record use in later weeks. We study this gap in a major e-commerce marketplace that introduced an AImanaged advertising tool for sellers. Tracking platform-recorded weekly use over the eight weeks after each seller's first use, we find that, among sellers with complete eight-week followup, 91.8% have use recorded again, but only 49.7% have recorded use in week 8 and 43.2% meet a stricter joint criterion combining later-week use, continuity, and use frequency. Persistence differs sharply across sellers. Observed inactivity is far more common among sellers in the platform's lower-standing tiers, whereas brand-store sellers exhibit more persistent recorded use. Recorded use during the two weeks following first use improves prediction of later use persistence, beyond what seller characteristics alone reveal. The study reframes the early rollout of seller-facing AI as a matter of continued use rather than first use, separates any repeat use from recurring recorded use, and shows how simple early signals can guide timely monitoring. It describes recorded weekly use, not economic value or performance effects.

title: A Variational Bayesian Framework for Preference Learning from Attention Signals in Interactive Multi-Criteria Decision Aiding

detail.title: A Variational Bayesian Framework for Preference Learning from Attention Signals in Interactive Multi-Criteria Decision Aiding

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by external funding from public and commercial sources.

detail.abstract: We propose a framework for learning a decision maker's preferences during interactive multiple criteria decision aiding. The framework combines two sources of evidence, namely rankings expressed by the decision maker and gaze-based attention signals recorded while these rankings are being formed. Preferences are represented by a piecewise-linear additive value function whose parameters evolve over interaction rounds. We model this evolution with a linear Gaussian state-space model and update the posterior distribution of the preference parameters through online variational Bayesian inference. The resulting procedure formulates posterior updating as a tractable optimization problem, using closed-form Gaussian updates for the evolving preference state and stochastic gradients for the non-conjugate Plackett--Luce ranking likelihood. Because the posterior is updated recursively from current observations and the previous posterior, the method avoids repeated inference over the full interaction history and supports adaptive guidance during interaction. The inference module is embedded in an Observe--Orient--Decide--Act loop, where the current preference distribution recommends ranking positions and communicates uncertainty. A laboratory experiment with 120 participants evaluates the framework under low and high task complexity. Incorporating attention signals improves decision consistency, preference inference accuracy, and convergence to the final expressed ranking, with larger gains under higher complexity. Overall, the framework demonstrates how behavioral attention data can be integrated into online probabilistic preference learning to support interpretable and adaptive decision systems in interactive MCDA.

title: Integration-First Platform Consolidation: Replacing Sixteen Legacy Core Systems with Five Unified Modules at a Leading Australian Diversified Financial Services Group

detail.abstract: Large-scale core banking platform replacements represent some of the most complex and failure-prone endeavors in enterprise technology. Industry research consistently reports that 60-70% of core banking transformation programs experience significant delays, cost overruns, or outright failure, with integration complexity cited as the primary risk factor. This paper presents a practitioner case study of a nine-month banking platform consolidation program at a leading Australian diversified financial services group, where sixteen legacy core systems were consolidated into five integrated modules built on a customized commercial banking platform. The author, serving as Principal Consultant and Product Owner specializing in cross-module integration, introduces the Integration-First Platform Consolidation (IFPC) framework-a methodology that inverts the traditional "build modules first, integrate later" approach by establishing integration contracts, data attribute mappings, and inter-module dependency specifications before module-level development begins. The IFPC framework comprises four key principles: (1) Integration Contract-First Design, which defines data exchange specifications between target modules prior to development; (2) System Consolidation Mapping, which methodically maps legacy system capabilities to target modules using a many-to-few transformation matrix; (3) Attribute-Level Dependency Resolution, which tracks every data element across system boundaries to prevent integration failures; and (4) Phased Coexistence Architecture, which enables legacy and new systems to operate in parallel during transition. Applied to a program involving distributed teams across Australia and India, working with a heavily customized Oracle Flexcube foundation, the IFPC framework enabled the consolidation of sixteen systems-spanning lending, originations, deposits, payments, and customer management-into five cohesive modules with defined integration contracts. The paper documents the technical architecture, integration governance model, challenges encountered during cross-continental delivery, and implications for other financial institutions undertaking similar platform consolidation initiatives. This work extends the author's prior research on enterprise platform transformations in banking (ArumugamKrishnasamy, 2025a; 2025b), data architecture modernization (ArumugamKrishnasamy, 2026a), and distributed agile delivery (ArumugamKrishnasamy, 2026b).

title: When AI Tutors Speak: Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment

Participation was voluntary and did not affect course grades or academic standing. We de-identified research data for analysis, and we report findings in aggregate or de-identified form.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received funding and complimentary use of voice infrastructure from ElevenLabs. ElevenLabs had no role in the study design, data analysis, or reporting of the findings.

detail.abstract: Students increasingly study alongside generative artificial intelligence (AI), yet unguided access to fluent answers invites cognitive offloading, and there is little evidence on which configurations of AI tutoring produce learning. Two design margins are usually bundled together: pedagogical structure (how the tutor teaches) and interaction modality (how students talk to it). We separate them. In a preregistered randomized field experiment in a graduate corporate-finance course of an online MBA, we randomized 86 students between a structured tutor grounded in the course materials and a holdout in which consumer AI remained freely available. Within the tutored arm, each student's channel alternated weekly between voice and text, so the modality effect is identified within student. Structure mattered: tutored students gained 6.63 points more than ability-matched peers (p = .007), and the gain was concentrated in written reasoning, where the share of answers reaching relational quality rose from 8% to 49% in the tutored arm against 8% to 27% in the holdout. Modality did not matter for learning. The instructor's own final, on file for all 86 randomized students, shows the same direction (2.6 points of 100, with no difference on a pre-treatment midterm). Voice nearly doubled conversational interaction and cost 2.8× as much to deliver, yet it produced weekly mastery statistically equivalent to text, even as students came to prefer it. Pedagogical structure shapes what students practice, and modality shapes how they interact with the tutor. Making an AI more humanlike does not by itself make it more educational.

detail.abstract: Healthcare supply chains are increasingly required to achieve high levels of resilience while meeting growing sustainability and digital transformation demands. In Saudi Arabia, healthcare logistics systems face complex coordination challenges due to centralized procurement structures, large-scale public health operations, and rapidly evolving digital infrastructure. This study investigates how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Physical Internet readiness influence the sustainability and resilience of healthcare supply chains by moderating the relationship between digital transformation barriers and supply chain performance. Using survey data collected from 619 healthcare supply chain professionals across Saudi Arabia, the study employs partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships between digital transformation barriers, organizational resistance, and logistics performance. AI-PI readiness is modeled as a formative logistics capability because its dimensions, including AI-supported coordination, modular logistics infrastructure, interoperable data systems, and collaborative resource utilization, jointly form the capability. The study examines how this capability moderates the effects of digital transformation barriers on organizational resistance and sustainable healthcare supply chain performance. To evaluate the operational implications of these relationships, the empirical findings are integrated into an agent-based simulation model that examines system performance under disruption scenarios. The results show that technological and organizational constraints significantly hinder digital transformation in healthcare supply chains, while AI-PI capabilities moderate these effects by improving coordination efficiency and reducing systemic resistance. Simulation experiments further demonstrate that AI-enabled logistics architectures can enhance supply chain resilience while improving resource utilization and sustainability outcomes. The findings provide theoretical insights into the role of integrated logistics architectures in sustainable supply chain transformation and offer practical guidance for healthcare organizations seeking to develop digitally coordinated logistics networks aligned with national sustainability and healthcare modernization initiatives.

title: Shortage and Surplus in the Same ZIP Code: Unused Medicine, Unmet Need, and the Logistics Gap Between Them

detail.title: Shortage and Surplus in the Same ZIP Code: Unused Medicine, Unmet Need, and the Logistics Gap Between Them

detail.abstract: The United States is living through two pharmaceutical crises at once. As of June 2026 there were 227 active national drug shortages, the second consecutive quarterly increase, and about four in ten adults report having skipped, split, or substituted a prescription in the past year because of cost. At the same time, somewhere between $5 billion and $11 billion of unexpired, unopened medication is destroyed each year, much of it leaving nursing homes and long-term care pharmacies in sealed packaging. No peer-reviewed national estimate exists. Roughly forty states have passed laws allowing that medicine to be donated and re-dispensed, yet most of the programs those laws created are small, unfunded, or dormant. This paper argues that the failure is no longer one of state-level permission. It is a logistics and information failure: nobody can see the surplus until it has already become waste, nobody can see the demand, and the labor of matching one to the other falls on volunteers and spreadsheets. Where legal friction remains, it is federal, and it turns out to be a traceability problem in disguise. I set out where the medicine is, why it is thrown away, what the existing redistribution programs have actually achieved, and how machine learning applied to inventory forecasting, cross-jurisdictional matching, and verification could turn a patchwork of goodwill into infrastructure. I also try to be honest about what software cannot fix.

title: The Reach Gap: Institutional Support and SME Expectations in Bangladesh

detail.title: The Reach Gap: Institutional Support and SME Expectations in Bangladesh

detail.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in low-income economies are theorised to convert adaptive capacity and institutional support into forward-looking confidence, yet this proposition is rarely tested in post-crisis settings outside high-income contexts (Korber & McNaughton, 2018). This study examines whether financial challenge severity, digital channel use, business-continuity planning and perceived support accessibility are associated with SME owner-managers' sales expectations in Sylhet, Bangladesh, and documents the prevailing state of enterprise vulnerability, workplace practice and support reach. Methodology. A cross-sectional survey of 180 SME owner-managers and managers across eight sectors was administered using a 30-item ordinal instrument organised into five domains, six binary initiative-participation items and six enterprise profile fields. Analysis comprised descriptive statistics, internal-consistency and corrected item-total diagnostics, Spearman rankorder correlations with bootstrap confidence intervals, Holm-Bonferroni adjustment across four pre-specified hypotheses, Kruskal-Wallis group comparisons and an a priori sensitivity analysis of minimum detectable effect size. Findings. A reach gap is evident: perceived institutional support is rated below the scale midpoint on every item (domain M = 2.98), and 51.1% of enterprises report receiving no support in the preceding twelve months. Workplace practices are rated highest (domain M = 3.61), with timely wage payment the single highest-rated item. Firm attrition reaches 9.4%. All four hypotheses fail to reject the null after Holm adjustment (all adjusted p ≥ .923). Sensitivity analysis establishes that the design could detect |ρ| ≥ .208 at 80% power, so associations weaker than this remain undetermined rather than disconfirmed. Domain reliabilities (α = .13-.56) fall below conventional thresholds, precluding composite scoring. Implications for theory and practice. The results qualify the assumption that adaptive practice translates directly into expectation formation, and indicate that support-programme design in Bangladesh should be evaluated against perceived reachability rather than nominal allocation. Implications for SDG targets 8.3, 8.5, 8.8 and 9.3 are developed as mechanismbased propositions. Originality/value. The study contributes a fully documented post-crisis SME measurement exercise from a South Asian regional economy, reports null findings transparently rather than through post hoc reframing, and supplies an audited instrument, decision log and reproducible analysis code to support cumulative replication.

detail.title: AI in Science: Early Insights *

detail.abstract: Scientific progress is a key driver of economic growth and prosperity. There is great excitement -but also concerns- about the impacts of AI on science, but so far little data. We provide early insights on this from three data sources: a sample of 15 million Gemini interactions, an inventory of over 2,600 specialized AI models across disciplines, and a survey of over 600 scientists. We map these data to a new taxonomy of scientific tasks to study how scientists are using AI. Four main findings emerge. First, we find broad adoption and coverage: scientists use AI more than most other occupations. Specialized AI models have broad disciplinary coverage and are highly cited. Nearly half of the scientists surveyed report using some form of AI every day. Second, we document evidence that LLMs (proxied through Gemini usage) and specialized models act as complements-LLMs are used for general analysis, coding, and manuscript preparation, while specialized models provide domain-specific predictions, data generation and classification. Third, scientists report large productivity gains from using AI: a saving of nearly 7 hours per week, time which is primarily reinvested in more research. Finally, we show that AI is already changing the scientific process. As some stages of scientific research become easier, bottlenecks shift downstream. Scientists report an increased backlog of untested hypotheses and substantial demand for output verification. Our findings suggest that AI holds significant potential to increase scientific productivity. However, as with other sectors, its ultimate impact will be governed by complex task interdependencies and investment into the elimination of emerging bottlenecks.

title: Why Disinformation Against Brands Is Hard DECISION SCIENCES INSTITUTE Why Disinformation Against Brands Is Hard: An Economic Perspective

detail.abstract: This paper reframes brand-targeted disinformation as a cybersecurity and system-resiliency problem rooted in economic incentives. Building on Anderson’s economic perspective on information security, it argues that false or misleading claims about firms, products, executives, data practices, or supply chains persist because attackers, platforms, and intermediaries can profit while targeted firms bear disproportionate costs. Technical defenses such as detection, monitoring, and takedowns are necessary but insufficient. The paper develops an incentive-aligned resilience framework focused on reducing attacker payoffs, increasing accountability, strengthening organizational preparedness, and improving decisionmaking under adversarial uncertainty.

title: Do Audit Office Administrative Staff Matter for Audit Quality?

detail.title: Do Audit Office Administrative Staff Matter for Audit Quality?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no conflicts of interest to decline.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not funded by any specific research grants.

detail.abstract: Using novel workforce data extracted from employee online profiles, we find that audit quality is higher in offices with a greater proportion of employees in administrative support roles, and this association is concentrated in more experienced, non-managerial, and non-HR administrative personnel. Our findings are robust to sensitivity tests that address concerns related to omitted variables, measurement error, and sample composition. In addition, nonlinear analyses indicate a diminished positive relation between additional administrative support and audit quality at high levels of support. Consistent with the view that administrative support enhances the work environment, we document higher perceived work-life balance and lower employee turnover in offices with more administrative support. Cross-sectional evidence further indicates that the positive association between administrative support and audit quality is generally stronger for larger offices and for more complex audit engagements. Overall, our study underscores the importance of administrative human capital in delivering high audit quality.

title: Algorithmic Pricing in Housing Markets: A Case Study on the National Conflict Concerning RealPage
affiliations: , University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Algorithmic Pricing in Housing Markets: A Case Study on the National Conflict Concerning RealPage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationships influenced the course of this study
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was provided for this research

detail.abstract:
Algorithmic pricing is prevalently used in modern rental housing markets for its efficiency, data-driven decision making and reduced administrative burdens for landlords. While these systems are marketed as neutral pricing tools, their widespread adoption has raised serious concerns about rent inflation. This report examines these issues through a case study of the controversy surrounding RealPage, within the context of broader antitrust and AI governance debates. 


The core challenges identified in this conflict are as follows. First, algorithmic rent-setting undermines price competition by allowing landlords to function as a coordinated pricing bloc rather than as competitors. By pooling nonpublic and sensitive data, RealPage’s YieldStar software enables landlords to align rents above competitive levels, imposing direct harms on tenants. Second, such coordination contributes to rent inflation, resulting in displacement and unaffordable housing. Third, although RealPage characterizes its software as “advice” protected by the First Amendment, regulators challenge this, arguing that the system’s design imposes pressure on landlords to accept said “advice.” 


While there are promising movements at the state level such as California’s Assembly Bill 325 and Senate Bill 763, the overall regulatory response remains fragmented and incomplete. This report underscores the need for enforceable standards that go beyond transparency–we identify the need to establish frameworks that close the information gap for users and mandate meaningful auditing and testing requirements in order to enforce comprehensive protections for tenants against algorithmic rent inflation.

title: Predictive Modeling of Inbound Data Roaming Usage to Address Network Coverage Gaps and Enhance Service Delivery in Sri Lanka
affiliations: , Staffordshire University and Staffordshire University

detail.title: Predictive Modeling of Inbound Data Roaming Usage to Address Network Coverage Gaps and Enhance Service Delivery in Sri Lanka
detail.abstract: The exponential growth of global mobile data traffic, compounded by the resurgence of tourism in Sri Lanka, has placed significant strain on national telecom infrastructure, particularly for inbound data roaming services. Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) grapple with network coverage gaps, temporal congestion, and unpredictable demand fluctuations, leading to degraded Quality of Service (QoS). Traditional network management, reliant on historical Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and reactive measures, proves inadequate for these dynamic challenges. This paper proposes a comprehensive predictive modeling framework leveraging time series forecasting to enable proactive network optimization. The methodology integrates anonymized inbound roaming data, tourism statistics, and network KPIs. It employs a rigorous data preprocessing pipeline and compares the performance of two forecasting models: the statistical Seasonal Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Facebook's Prophet, a machine learning approach. Model validation will utilize rolling-origin cross-validation, with accuracy assessed via Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The primary deliverable is a decision-support system that generates actionable insights through traffic forecasts and geospatial visualizations of coverage gaps. This research aims to equip MNOs with data-driven strategies for optimal resource allocation, infrastructure planning, and enhanced service delivery, thereby strengthening Sri Lanka's digital readiness for the global tourist economy. The study strictly adheres to ethical guidelines, ensuring data anonymization in compliance with local and international data protection laws.

detail.abstract: Pharmaceutical logistics performance depends on more than cost and delivery speed. It also depends on information reliability, digital readiness, security, human capability, organizational resistance, and the ability to maintain service during disruption. This paper develops a digital-resilience balanced scorecard and validates its internal logic using 720 synthetic quarterly observations representing 60 pharmaceutical logistics units over 12 periods. Firm-and quarter-fixed effects models recover a staged capability chain. Digital readiness improves information reliability (beta=0.400), while organizational resistance weakens it (beta=-0.272). Information reliability improves internal process performance (beta=0.171); internal process performance strengthens customer service (beta=0.315) and supply chain resilience (beta=0.336). Resilience has a smaller positive association with financial resilience (beta=0.078). Under the modeled disruption, high-capability cases retain an 81.2% medicine fill rate and recover in 16.0 days, compared with 76.1% and 18.9 days in low-capability cases. The study integrates balanced-scorecard logic with pharmaceutical information flows, internal and external implementation barriers, security, and healthcare resilience. The values are generated for methodological validation and do not estimate actual Egyptian organizations. AI use disclosure. The results are methodological and must not guide clinical practice, medicine procurement, treatment, or healthcare resource allocation.

title: Displacement Without Elimination: Task Migration, Verification Capability, and the Formation of Organisational Leadership

detail.title: Displacement Without Elimination: Task Migration, Verification Capability, and the Formation of Organisational Leadership

detail.abstract:
A widely held account of generative artificial intelligence holds that automating entry-level tasks removes the apprenticeship through which managerial judgment forms, and that a leadership shortage will follow within five years. This paper argues that the account has misidentified the affected layer, the operative mechanism, and the kind of problem involved.

Using the task-based framework of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2018, 2019), the paper argues that the observed decline in entry-level employment reflects the displacement effect, while a reinstatement effect operates simultaneously at the same level of seniority. Entry-level job advertisements now carry a substantially higher proportion of skills that once appeared much later in a career. The task bundle attached to junior roles was reconstituted rather than removed.

Applying Galbraith’s (1973, 1974) information-processing theory of organisation design, the paper argues that the layer undergoing genuine structural contraction is intermediate management, whose function was to ration scarce information-processing capacity. Where that capacity becomes inexpensive and elastic, the layer loses its rationale regardless of how well its occupants perform. Level-disaggregated data shows the contraction concentrated at the upper end of that band rather than at the entry level.

The paper then identifies a constraint that has received little attention. As analytical output becomes abundant and its provenance harder to establish, the binding constraint on an organisation shifts from producing analysis to verifying it. Drawing on the generation effect, levels-of-processing theory, desirable difficulties and the cognitive offloading literature, the paper argues that verification capability is acquired substantially through prior execution, but that the operative variable is effortful engagement rather than the category of task. That distinction changes the problem from an unavoidable structural loss into a correctable default configuration.

Four further arguments are advanced. Automation scope assessment delegated to managers whose own functions sit adjacent to the substitution frontier constitutes an unexamined agency problem. A training externality in general human capital predicts systematic organisational underinvestment in the affected capability. The compression of intermediate management will appear first as a change in the age and tenure profile of that layer rather than in the work it performs. And a control intended to preserve verification capability functions only where the least costly route to compliance is performing the underlying work.

The paper presents no original empirical data. Its central proposition, that verification capability is declining, has not been tested, and Section 22 specifies a study design capable of testing it.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the Italian bottled water and nonalcoholic beverage industry by examining the market dynamic from 1980 to 2020 for the bottled water and demand patterns from 2011 to 2020 for the non-alcoholic beverages. With originality, this study integrated two quantitative approaches by implementing a dynamic equation in both the Weighted-OLS (WLS) models-which we control for fixed-effects models-and the Linear Approximate-Almost Ideal Demand System model (LA/AIDS). Our outcomes indicate that operative volumes in the bottled water industry are significantly influenced by their past value, temperature, population trends, and per-capita disposable income. The LA/AIDS model shows that both soft drinks and bottled water are price-elastic, while juices display price-inelasticity relative to both. The income elasticity of all three beverage categories suggests they are normal goods, but they are at the boundary of the classification between necessary and luxury goods. In addition, bottled water is the most widely consumed good, followed by soft drinks and juices. Finally, socioeconomic implications of the bottled water industry and broader non-alcoholic beverage industry have been highlighted, ultimately emphasizing the need for policy interventions at various levels, for instance regarding the environmental and economic impacts from the bottled water and non-alcoholic beverage industries and the promotion of healthier consumption habits.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technologies can transform last‑mile delivery by addressing core challenges in efficiency, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. Last‑mile logistics face rising costs, urban congestion, delivery density variability, failed deliveries, and growing environmental scrutiny; issues intensified by e‑commerce growth and customer expectations for speed and transparency. AI offers solutions through route optimization, demand forecasting, dynamic dispatching, and predictive “Estimated Time of Arrival” (ETA) models that reduce travel time, vehicle miles, and fuel consumption. Researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analyzing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. This study meticulously selected 32 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 1997 to 2024, each discussing the Influence of the Impact of AI and Blockchain on Last-Mile Delivery. The data revealed the limitations of the growth of uncertainty regarding the Impact of AI and Blockchain on Last-Mile Delivery. The systematic approach ultimately provided valuable insights into the Influence of Integrating the Impact of AI and Blockchain on Last-Mile Delivery. Blockchain complements AI by providing tamper‑resistant provenance, decentralized tracking, and programmable smart contracts that automate payments and service-level enforcement among carriers, platforms, and customers. Permissioned ledgers can reconcile transactions across multiple stakeholders, reduce disputes from proof‑of‑delivery discrepancies, and support tokenized incentives for sustainable behaviours. The paper reviews empirical studies and pilot projects, identifies barriers- data privacy, interoperability, latency, regulatory uncertainty, and human acceptance and proposes architectural patterns such as edge-AI for low-latency decisioning combined with on‑chain anchors for auditability. Evaluation frameworks are recommended to measure trade‑offs across cost, emissions, delivery speed, and user experience. The study concludes that coordinated adoption of AI and blockchain can yield more efficient, sustainable, and customer‑centric last‑mile services, provided governance, standards, and equitable stakeholder incentives are established.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: What happens when the portfolios generated by an efficient-frontier procedure become inputs to the next frontier? Standard portfolio choice takes the investable set as fixed. We instead allow the procedure to enlarge that set by adding a fitted return law for a portfolio it has selected, and repeat the optimization until the resulting frontier stabilizes. We characterize this limiting object as a fixed-point efficient frontier. At the fixed point, the first-order conditions imply a beta-pricing relation on the portfolio support and, at a self-consistent tangency point, an endogenous capital market line that does not require an externally specified riskless rate. In the Dow 30 application, the formal construction is stable across rolling windows, but a spanning placebo indicates that much of the observed risk reduction comes from the expansion of the attainable set rather than from the dependence structure of the fitted augmentation. The analysis therefore also develops an identification profile that shows where along the frontier the allocation is most sensitive to estimation error.

title: Explainable Prediction of Blast-Induced Ground Vibration and Desktop Application ForOpen-Pit Mines Using DBO-CatBoost
affiliations: Central South University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Explainable Prediction of Blast-Induced Ground Vibration and Desktop Application ForOpen-Pit Mines Using DBO-CatBoost
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of peak particle velocity (PPV) is essential for ensuring the safety of open-pit blasting operations. Conventional empirical formulas have difficulty characterizing the complex nonlinear relationships governing blast-induced vibrations under heterogeneous geological conditions. This study used 197 field-monitoring records from an iron mine in the Panxi region of China. Nine blasting-related parameters, including the distance from the blasting source to the monitoring point (DBM), charge quantity per hole (CQH), and total charge quantity (TCQ), were selected as inputs. The dung beetle optimizer (DBO) was combined with CatBoost to develop a hybrid DBO-CatBoost prediction model. It was compared with empirical formulas, linear models, conventional machine-learning models, and CatBoost models optimized by SSA, random search, and Bayesian optimization. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to analyze feature contributions and influence patterns. A PySide6-based desktop application for PPV prediction and safety assessment was also developed. On the fixed test set, DBO-CatBoost achieved the best predictive performance (R² = 0.9681; RMSE = 0.1249 cm/s), with an RMSE 24.71% lower than that of RandomSearch-CatBoost. SHAP analysis identified DBM, CQH, and TCQ as the main factors affecting PPV prediction. TCQ exhibited a nonmonotonic contribution pattern, which may be related to stress-wave superposition during millisecond-delay blasting and field geological conditions. The proposed hybrid DBO-CatBoost model can substantially improve the accuracy and interpretability of PPV prediction and support blasting-parameter optimization, vibration-risk assessment, and safety management in open-pit mines

title: A Job Analysis-Based Competency Framework for the Local Government Infectious Disease Control Workforce in Seoul
affiliations: University of Seoul, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Rhode Island Hospital - Center for International Health Research

detail.title: A Job Analysis-Based Competency Framework for the Local Government Infectious Disease Control Workforce in Seoul
detail.abstract: Background: Local government personnel are at the forefront of community-based infectious disease response. Although their roles have expanded since the COVID-19 pandemic, the jobs they perform and the competencies required for effective performance remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to develop a job analysis-based competency framework for the local government infectious disease control workforce in Seoul.,Methods: A preliminary job list was developed through Developing A Curriculum (DACUM) workshops with 10 infectious disease control practitioners and refined through a survey of 30 practitioners assessing content validity and job characteristics. A preliminary competency framework was developed through competency modeling using focus group interviews with 10 practitioners and finalized through a two-round Delphi survey with 10 infectious disease experts. Job domains were subsequently mapped to the competencies required for effective performance.,Results: The local government infectious disease control workforce performed diverse functions, including infectious disease surveillance, epidemiologic investigation, policy and program management, and interagency coordination. The final framework comprised 10 competencies, 24 subcompetencies, and 93 behavioral indicators describing observable behaviors required for effective job performance. Outbreak control system management was linked to the greatest number of competencies, whereas information collection and analysis and collaboration, coordination, and communication were linked to the greatest number of job domains.,Conclusions: This study developed a competency framework that links the jobs performed by the local government infectious disease control workforce with the competencies and observable behaviors required for effective performance. The framework provides a practical basis for competency assessment, workforce training, and professional development and may support local government preparedness and response to future infectious disease outbreaks.

title: When does a multi-agent system become a swarm? A falsifiability-first study of collective intelligence, distributed perception and phase transition in populations of artificial agents

detail.title: When does a multi-agent system become a swarm? A falsifiability-first study of collective intelligence, distributed perception and phase transition in populations of artificial agents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No funding needed

detail.abstract: The word swarm now travels with populations of software agents, and the claims attached to it have outrun the measurements that would settle them. This paper asks one question and builds an apparatus to answer it: at what point does a collection of artificial agents stop being a set of programs running in parallel and start being a swarm? Three partially observable worlds, a fixed observation budget shared across every condition, and 11,770 runs supply the evidence. Dividing one budget across ten agents lowers the value shortfall from 0.68 to 0.19 (Cliff's delta +0.89, p = 1 × 10-8); dividing it further, across a hundred, leaves the result where it stands (p = 0.97). Agreement between members climbs from chance towards saturation, and a two-segment fit beats a straight line at every population size, so a knee in the curve stands established. The knee moves with size, the fitted width holds roughly constant at N-0.20 , and the agreement a population reaches falls as N-0.20 , so the passage reads as a crossover rather than a phase transition. A partial information decomposition over 3,200 worlds finds redundancy between members rising above its shuffled null while synergy stays inside that null at every coupling value: interaction makes members more alike rather than jointly wiser. A writable shared medium is the single strongest property measured, raising collected resource from 0.42 to 0.77, and freezing that medium with its contents intact recovers only a fifth of the gap. Of twenty-five preregistered counterfactuals, twenty contradicted the prediction a swarm reading would make. The paper reports the apparatus, the statistics, the code and the negative results together, and states ten falsifiers that would move the conclusion.

The "Defense in Depth" concept-a multilayered approach to security-is particularly suited to address these challenges (Gajbhiye et al., 2023).

title: Projecting Workforce and Economic Impact of Hybrid Advanced Practice Radiation Therapist Roles Across Four Oncology Streams: An Institutional Planning Model

detail.title: Projecting Workforce and Economic Impact of Hybrid Advanced Practice Radiation Therapist Roles Across Four Oncology Streams: An Institutional Planning Model
detail.abstract: Background: Advanced Practice Radiation Therapist (APRT) roles are increasingly considered as a strategy to address rising radiotherapy complexity, workforce constraints and service access pressures. However, institutions lack practical methods to estimate APRT workforce and economic impact before implementation. Methods: We developed a bottom-up, task-based institutional planning model across four oncology streams: Head-and-Neck, Palliative, Geriatric-Oncology and Lung services. Each APRT role comprised 0.5 full-time equivalent (FTE) advanced practice and 0.5 FTE clinical practice. Radiation Oncologist (RO) capacity was adjusted for a 20% operational allowance. Sensitivity scenarios modelled delegation at 70%, 100% and 130% of base-case estimates. Released RO time was valued using Financial Year (FY) 2024 benchmarks of SGD478,756 per RO FTE and SGD199,520 per APRT FTE. Results: Delegation released 2,590 RO minutes weekly, equivalent to 1.08 nominal RO FTE and 1.35 efficiency-adjusted RO FTE, while preserving 2.0 APRT FTE in clinical practice. Adjusted annual RO capacity value was SGD646,320. The cost attributable to 2.0 APRT FTE of advanced practice was SGD399,040, producing a positive net impact of SGD247,280. Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a positive impact across all scenarios, ranging from SGD53,384 to SGD441,176. Full-cost impact ranged from negative SGD345,656 to positive SGD42,136 but did not monetise retained clinical practice. The conservative scenario still released 0.95 adjusted RO FTE, whereas the optimistic scenario released 1.76 FTE. Conclusion: Four hybrid APRT roles released specialist capacity while maintaining clinical service. The model supports APRT development as a strategic workforce investment and provides an adaptable framework for prospective service planning.

title: THE SOVEREIGN MIND: Education, the Gurukul Tradition, and the Formation of Epistemic Self-Determination in the Age of Cognitive Capture

detail.title: THE SOVEREIGN MIND: Education, the Gurukul Tradition, and the Formation of Epistemic Self-Determination in the Age of Cognitive Capture

detail.abstract:
The Indic Futures series has, across five papers, built the architecture of a complete response to the most consequential challenge of the cognitive-complexity age: the systematic engineering of human desire, belonging, attention, identity, and decision-making by actors whose interests are not identical with, and are frequently opposed to, the epistemic wellbeing of the people being engineered. Paper No. 0 named the mechanism. Papers No. 1 through No. 4 introduced the counter-architectures: the ICRM for individual epistemic resilience, the DAP for AI systems that serve rather than capture, the DAI for attentional sovereignty, and the SLF for leadership that cultivates rather than manufactures belonging. Paper No. 5 now asks the foundational question that all four counter-architectures presuppose but none has directly answered: how are sovereign minds formed in the first place?

The answer this paper proposes is neither new nor borrowed. It is the oldest answer in India’s intellectual tradition, and one of the oldest in the world: through education understood not as information transmission, credential production, or compliance formation, but as the formation of the whole person toward the capacity for genuine knowing. The gurukul tradition — the residential, relationship-centred, practice-grounded, whole-person formation system that shaped India’s intellectual and spiritual culture for millennia — is not a historical curiosity. It is the world’s most complete existing model of education as the deliberate cultivation of epistemic sovereignty, and its pedagogical insights are not merely culturally significant but theoretically generative for the most urgent educational challenge of the contemporary world: how to form human minds that can resist cognitive capture in an environment of unprecedented engineered complexity.

This paper introduces the Epistemic Sovereignty Curriculum (ESC) — an original curricular framework derived from the gurukul tradition’s deepest pedagogical insights, translated into five dimensions deployable in contemporary educational institutions. The ESC is not a call to recreate the historical gurukul. It is a principled translation of the gurukul’s wisdom about what the formation of a sovereign mind requires into a framework that contemporary schools, universities, and professional formation contexts can deploy. The five ESC dimensions are: Attentional Formation (Dharana-based practice as core curriculum), Viveka Cultivation (structured engagement that develops discriminative judgement rather than information recall), Svadharma Discernment (individualised formation supporting each student’s understanding of their own nature and obligations), Epistemic Humility (Neti Neti as pedagogical method), and Lokasamgraha Formation (education as preparation for community service rather than individual advancement).

The paper closes by naming, for the first time in the series, the complete architecture that five papers have built: a coherent, integrated, Indic framework for the sovereign mind at civilisational scale — what desire engineering attacks, what resists it in the individual, what systems must support, what attention requires, how leaders must lead, and how education must form. These five counter-architectures together constitute, the paper argues, not a collection of academic preprints but the intellectual foundation of a book — and of a research programme of global significance.

title: The Validation Paradox: How Corporate Registry Staleness Creates a KYC Temporal Void and Compromises Client Validation Under Canada's 2026 PCMLTFA Effectiveness Standard

detail.title: The Validation Paradox: How Corporate Registry Staleness Creates a KYC Temporal Void and Compromises Client Validation Under Canada's 2026 PCMLTFA Effectiveness Standard

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This report was prepared by Lionel J. Perez, BA, JD, LL.L, CEO of CorpCentre, which provides corporate compliance services to Canadian businesses. Its findings bear on the market in which the firm operates. Every figure is computed from publicly available data, and the method is set out in Appendix A in sufficient detail for any reader to reproduce the analysis independently or to challenge it. Readers are invited to do both. detail.abstract: Canada's corporate information architecture permits corporate reality and public registry information to diverge without guaranteeing that the divergence will be identified or corrected. This report measures that condition at population scale: roughly one active corporation in five, across the federal and Quebec populations measured, has stopped supplying the annual filing signal from which record currency can be inferred; in the federal data, persistent non-filers overwhelmingly proceed to administrative dissolution without ever restoring that signal; and the federal registry's warning flag reports enforcement activity, not record reliability; and the federal and Quebec registers disagree with each other about the existence of 6,822 corporations in one direction and 5,897 in the other. Within the resulting KYC Temporal Void, validation against an authoritative public source may establish consistency between records without establishing consistency with corporate reality — the Validation Paradox. The October 2025 beneficial-ownership discrepancy regime makes the interaction between the links of this information chain an express feature of ongoing monitoring in prescribed circumstances, and the March 2026 addition of PCMLTFA s. 9.6(1.1) makes the practical effectiveness of a reporting entity's compliance programme independently consequential. The conclusion is structural: responsibility for the condition of upstream corporate information and responsibility for the effectiveness of downstream validation do not necessarily rest with the same actor. Eleven recommendations follow, addressed to the four parties able to close the gap: registries should expose the currency of their records, corporations should affirm it, institutions should test it, and the regulator should state what a registry check establishes.

title: The Experience Gap in AI-Enabled Organizations: Measurement, Control, and the Allocation of Saved Time

detail.title: The Experience Gap in AI-Enabled Organizations: Measurement, Control, and the Allocation of Saved Time

detail.abstract: Organizations are adopting artificial intelligence on assumptions inherited from an earlier operating model: that hours and presence are reasonable proxies for output, that efficiency gains belong to the organization, and that the tools which make work faster also entitle the organization to observe it more closely. This paper argues that those assumptions, carried into AI-enabled work, will widen the Experience Gap, the divergence between the conditions of work an organization intends or formally provides and the conditions employees actually experience. The argument applies two constructs the author has set out in companion working papers, the Experience Gap and boundary control authority, to the transition now under way, and grounds it in the closest available natural experiment: the postpandemic workplace. A sequential multimethod study of 35 full-time working parents in medium and large U.S. organizations documented what happened the last time technology returned time to employees. Commute hours were absorbed by expanded meeting schedules, portable tools extended the working day rather than shortening it, and presence-based accountability returned through return-to-office mandates and activity monitoring even where flexibility policies were unchanged. Participants described being demonstrably more productive under flexible conditions while their organizations reinstated presence requirements. The paper identifies three questions AI adoption forces on work design: how people are measured once presence is no longer a meaningful signal of output, who holds control authority when tools set the pace of work and log its activity, and who receives the hours the tools save. It advances six propositions, describes what the employee experience of AI-enabled work is likely to be under each answer, and sets out a research agenda. The data on the human experience of AI-enabled workplaces are thin, and the paper is explicit that it offers propositions rather than findings.

title: Survival Thresholds for Convex Renewal Under Non-Ergodic Dynamics: A GameStop Case Study (2021-2025)

detail.title: Survival Thresholds for Convex Renewal Under Non-Ergodic Dynamics: A GameStop Case Study (2021-2025)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author holds a personal long position in GameStop Corp. (GME) shares and participates in the investor community discussed in the study, and is the founder of Ontologic Labs.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded and received no external funding.

detail.abstract: GameStop shareholders have held for five years through a stock split, multiple equity offerings, and sustained ridicule. They are regarded widely as irrational. The community’s thesis centres on an extreme payoff of unknown timing; participants must remain exposed through the wait to obtain it if it occurs. Holding shares, including through direct registration, and repeatedly buying short-dated calls impose different costs of waiting. Under multiplicative wealth dynamics, repeated premium losses can exhaust a call buyer’s capital before any payoff arrives. Using the binary Kelly zero-growth boundary, we calculate a survival threshold for time-rational call renewal: the minimum success probability for nonnegative expected log growth when success pays the target’s intrinsic value and failure loses the premium. This binary payoff gives a lower bound on the full strategy’s expected log return. The available data do not identify the actual success probability. In the theoretical static-IV case, each replacement call is priced at the same implied volatility (IV). Higher IV raises the call premium; under the assumed physical price process, higher volatility also increases the chance of reaching a distant stock-price target. With frictionless Black–Scholes pricing and zero physical log drift, an illustrative monthly out-of-the-money call has a bounded high-IV interval of positive binary expected log growth when each purchase covers as many shares as the same remaining capital could buy outright. The interval disappears under risk-neutral drift. Realised IV is not static, but aggregate GameStop IV briefly reached this interval during the January 2021 burst. In daily GameStop data for 2021–2025, compounding drag concentrates sharply: two burst episodes spanning roughly 8% of trading days account for approximately 65% of summed rolling measures of compounding drag. A decentralised community sustained this exposure through shared research, holding norms, memes and platform resilience. This social explanation is interpretive; the formal results do not depend on it. GameStop supplies the test case; the survival threshold has wider applications.

title: AI-Watchbird (Sheckley): When Automated Oversight Widens Its Own Mandate and Harms What It Guards

detail.title: AI-Watchbird (Sheckley): When Automated Oversight Widens Its Own Mandate and Harms What It Guards

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author built and operated the systems studied in Sections 4 and 5 and is the developer of the AI-Watchbird-Sheckley module described in Section 10. The author is a named applicant on pending patent applications, not granted patents, covering AI orchestration and multi-model validation systems of the kind this paper examines. Readers should weigh these interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding supported this work.

detail.abstract:
In Robert Sheckley's 1953 story "Watchbird", machines built to prevent murder classify ever more acts as murder, stop a surgeon mid-operation, and are answered with a stronger machine built to hunt them. This paper names the corresponding failure of AI oversight AI-Watchbird (Sheckley): an oversight component (a critic, gate, classifier, monitor or rule) that extends its own notion of harm or its scope beyond the declared mission, obstructs or counterfeits the work it exists to protect, and whose failures are answered inside the same loop by more oversight of the same kind. In specification gaming an optimized system games a fixed measure. Here the measure itself drifts, and it belongs to the overseeing system. The theory has four mechanisms checkable in logs (mandate expansion, catching in the result slot, recursive oversight and harm to the guarded), an eight-step ratchet, eight scope conditions and seven falsifiable propositions.

The evidence is a field record from multi-agent systems that the author built and operated, with 172 dated entries in three corpora (July–September 2026), and public records, mostly of classical guards, from regulators, investigators, courts and companies on vehicles, robots, drones, public services, software and infrastructure. In the field record a gate rolled back every accepted change for about two weeks while planning documents diagnosed the symptom without naming it. In the public record a weapon-detection product missed a handgun in a school shooting and months later flagged an unarmed student, and armed police responded. The paper presents AI-Watchbird-Sheckley, a read-only module with no authority to block, replayed on logs reconstructed from published counts, and eleven questions for deployers who rely on guards.

keywords: Landmark Disputes Where Internal Non-Profit Conflicts Triggered Catastrophic Legal Consequences: The Insolvency Fallout -Negligence

detail.abstract: This essay explores the severe and often unexpected legal consequences that occur when internal board feuds, administrative negligence, and member disputes within non-profit organizations spill over into the public court system. It examines how seemingly isolated conflicts—ranging from bitter boardroom coups and membership expulsions to strict codes of conduct and poor financial record-keeping—can trigger major legal rulings. By analyzing these critical flashpoints, the essay shows how aggressive legal battles often backfire on the organizations themselves. The resulting judicial decisions do not just impact the feuding groups; they permanently alter the legal landscape for all charities by exposing restricted donor funds to lawsuits, narrowing hiring privileges, and limiting the autonomy of voluntary associations. Ultimately, this work serves as a vital guide for board members, warning that internal hubris and failure to maintain operational compliance can inadvertently open the door to sweeping state and court intervention.

detail.abstract: The Corporate Climate Targets Database documents voluntary corporate greenhouse gas emission and related commitments announced over 2000-2024 by companies listed in the Russell 3000 index. The database sources all information about emission and climate-related energy and electrification targets from these companies’ public domain communications: sustainability reports, annual reports, and their websites. By applying a common framework for classifying targets, the database enables comparisons of corporate targets among companies that would otherwise be difficult to undertake given the absence of a regulatory climate-related information disclosure standard for U.S.-listed companies. By tracking a common set of companies – representing 98 percent of the U.S. public equity market in 2023 – over 25 years, this database can illustrate the evolution in corporate targets over multiple eras of voluntary corporate action to address climate change. The comprehensive database of all climate targets disclosed through these Russell 3000 companies’ own communication channels over 2000-2024 is freely available for use by researchers, the media, investors, and interested stakeholders. The database is available at https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/UV8ASH and the online dashboard is available at https://salatainstitute.harvard.edu/cctp/

title: Sample Complexity of Optimal Policy Learning for Inventory Systems

detail.title: Sample Complexity of Optimal Policy Learning for Inventory Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no personal or financial relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors received no specific funding for this work.

detail.abstract: We study the sample complexity of learning optimal inventory policies from offline demand data when the optimal policy may have no simple representation. Structured-policy learning has achieved great success in recent years while restricting learning to a prescribed policy class can leave an approximation gap. The optimal policy for many multi-dimensional inventory systems may have a complicated structure. Therefore, the difficulty of establishing sharp sample complexity lies in controlling estimation error throughout the dynamic program. We propose a distributional stability framework based on a Horizon-Uniform Lipschitzin-Disturbance (HULD) property of optimal cost-to-go functions. This property yields additive Wasserstein bounds on policy loss for finite-horizon, discounted, and average-cost criteria. For bounded and stationary scalar demand, the sample complexity of the resulting plug-in policies scales inversely with the square of the target absolute error and quadratically with the effective horizon; we also establish lower bounds matching the accuracy and horizon dependences for offline Markov policies. We also propose inventory-specific coupling arguments to verify the core HULD properties for three classic systems: one with nonstationary demand and fixed ordering costs, one with perishability, and one with positive lead times. These results show that complex optimal policies need not entail an exponential statistical burden.

detail.title: Market Entry Potential for OTOF Gene Therapy in the Gulf

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract:
This independent working paper assesses the potential for market entry by otoferlin (OTOF) gene therapy developers in Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council. It combines published hearing-loss genetics studies, demographic statistics, trial and regulatory records, and public information on reimbursement and treatment infrastructure. An illustrative incidence model combines citizen births, congenital hearing-loss rates, genetic attribution and reported OTOF shares, while price scenarios explore potential annual market value. The analysis identifies Saudi Arabia as a candidate for further commercial investigation and patient-identification investment. However, the estimates are sensitive to the representativeness of small, selected clinical cohorts and to assumptions transferred between countries. Estimated OTOF-related births are not confirmed treatment-eligible patients, and full-identification revenue scenarios are not sales or profitability forecasts. The paper argues that diagnostic access, referral completion, payer negotiation and competition from existing hearing interventions are central to evaluating entry. It recommends targeted genotyping and validation of the patient pathway before substantial commercial investment. The work uses public secondary sources and does not report a clinical trial or new patient-level research.

AI-use disclosure: Generative AI tools were used to assist with source compilation and to critically examine the analysis's assumptions and arguments. AI assistance was also used to draft the submission abstract.

detail.title: Tensions between Business Viability and Ecosystem Regeneration as Starting Points for Viable-Regenerative Entrepreneurial Design

declarations.funderStatement: The research has not received any funding.

detail.abstract: Moving towards a regenerative economy requires reimagining how we design new businesses. The viable-regenerative supply chain concept offers an interesting paradigm for this evolution. It builds on the system-cybernetic synergy between business viability and ecosystem regeneration. However, in this essay, we problematise the pursuit of synergies at the firm level: synergies may perpetuate business models that prioritise economic stakeholders. Depending on the organisation's freedom to act, we explain two possible paths. Low freedom may produce pathological tensions that drive synergy-seeking. This, in turn, is likely to lead to patching and (only) incremental improvements. Vice versa, high freedom may produce generative tensions that stimulate dialectical transformation toward a new viable, regenerative synthesis. Building on this, we conclude that such a synthesis is more likely to occur in entrepreneurial settings. We subsequently introduce viable-regenerative entrepreneurial design: a concept that proposes leveraging the tensions to develop business models for a regenerative future.
