detail.abstract: Ghana’s ports handled 1,701,246 twenty-foot equivalent units in 2024, more than double the 2014 figure. Published evidence reports that imported goods take about fourteen days to clear the border, and tracking and tracing is the weakest of the country’s six logistics components. The usual reading is that the country needs more infrastructure and more reform. This paper reads it differently. Systems in daily use produce many potentially useful signals, although their completeness, accessibility, timeliness and predictive sufficiency have not yet been demonstrated. The search in Appendix D found no publicly documented Ghanaian system that integrates those signals into a decision while there is still time to act. Publicly documented deployed systems largely answer one question, which is where the cargo is. The search did not identify a system that also answers the two that matter next: what this delay will cost the operation waiting for the goods, and who should do what about it now. The paper specifies ResilienceGrid, a decision layer that sits on top of the systems a supply chain already runs rather than replacing them. It predicts a consequential event with measured uncertainty, far enough ahead for a response to be possible. It prices what that prediction means for the operation waiting downstream. It issues a ranked instruction to a named owner with a deadline, sent to whoever can actually carry it out. And it learns, from what was recommended, what was done and what followed. The argument draws on organisational information processing theory, on the supply chain resilience literature, and on the documented record of two decades of customs digitalisation in Ghana. The specification is detailed enough to build, criticise or replicate. It gives eight design requirements, and a five-layer architecture built around a see-predict-simulate-act-learn loop. It also gives the event schema, the rule for ranking responses, the gates a forecasting model must pass before it goes into service, a data feasibility assessment, and the design options considered and rejected. ResilienceGrid is worked through as a proposed twenty-four-month pilot on industrial and mining spare parts, with a transfer case to agricultural perishables and a border clearance feature. Its evaluation protocol, indicators and identification strategy are committed to in advance, including a commitment to publish negative results. The paper is equally clear about what it does not claim. The system has not been built, and no partner has agreed to host it. None of the component technologies is new. Data availability is assessed rather than demonstrated, and the assessment is not yet verified against sample extracts. And software cannot repair the political economy that absorbed two decades of transparency reform at Ghana Customs. Four stated results would show the proposition to be wrong.

title: A House That Survives Its Brain

detail.title: A House That Survives Its Brain

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding needed

detail.abstract: Two houses can hold the same area, the same address and the same comfort today, and hold entirely different futures. This paper builds one of them and measures the difference. A house is described as modules, relations, activity contracts and a safety constitution; a runtime reads rooms off the relations rather than from a plan; and intelligence is removed one layer at a time while the house is asked what it can still do. Across 122 modules and 124 relations, the two architectures are identical with every brain running, both carrying an activity capacity of 0.722. Removing the house brain leaves a house whose intelligence is spread through its modules at 0.676 and a house whose intelligence sits in one node at 0.000. With every brain gone, the spread house still carries 0.326, because its warmth, its air, its water and its doors arrive through a thermosiphon, a passive stack, mains pressure and a hinge. Reversibility is measured separately: a house whose joints release by hand and a house whose joints are bonded deliver the same activities today and differ by a factor of sixty-seven in a candidate reading of operational property, and by a factor of one hundred and sixty in the hours needed to take them apart. Fifty-two counterfactuals, twelve experiments, a buildable room-scale demonstrator, a runtime, an observatory page and a bill of materials travel with the paper. The composition throughout is multiplicative: a house whose structure stands, whose air moves, whose water runs and whose only exit is blocked is uninhabitable, and a weighted sum would keep that fact hidden.

detail.abstract: Digital transformation has fundamentally changed human resource management (HRM), shifting organisations from traditional administrative procedures to the adoption of integrated human resource information systems (HRIS), cloud-based solutions, workforce analytics, and technology-driven decisionmaking. The study applies a structured literature-based analysis and framework, drawing on research on e-HRM, HRIS, HR analytics, people analytics, digital HR strategy, technology acceptance, and organizational performance. The analysis shows key outcomes in HR process efficiency, employee productivity, decision-making quality, strategic HR involvement, workforce analytics capability, organisational performance, and technology acceptance. title: When digitally enabled circular economy transformation constrains itself: the DICE system dynamics framework

detail.abstract: Digital innovation (DI) has emerged as a key enabler of circular economy (CE) transformation. Yet, existing research has predominantly focused on individual digital technologies, organizational capabilities, and CE outcomes, providing limited explanation of how the underlying innovation processes become dynamically interconnected over time. Addressing this gap, this study develops the DICE system dynamics framework by extending the DICE mechanism architecture into an endogenous feedback model of digitally enabled CE transformation. Represented through an integrated causal loop diagram, the framework identifies nineteen analytically salient feedback loops organized into three interconnected dynamic domains: foundational enabling dynamics, core transformation dynamics, and transformation sustaining dynamics. The framework reveals that important constraints on transformation can be endogenously generated: as digitally enabled circular transformation develops, increasing ecosystem participation, circular activity, and accumulated transformation outcomes can generate coordination and operational burdens, governance and participation tensions, informational risks, infrastructure constraints, rebound effects, and path dependencies that regulate subsequent transformation. Digitally enabled CE transformation is thereby conceptualized as a recursive, feedback-driven process rather than a linear, technology-driven transition. By integrating mechanism-based theorizing with qualitative system dynamics, the study advances digital circular innovation and innovation management research from a structural explanation of constituent mechanisms toward a dynamic systems perspective. For innovation managers and ecosystem orchestrators, the framework shifts attention beyond external barriers toward anticipating and managing the self-generated constraints that can emerge as digital circular ecosystems develop. The study provides a foundation for future empirical examination and quantitative system dynamics simulation.

detail.abstract: The workplaces are not becoming easier. Employee well-being has ceased to be a sideline conversation as organisations increasingly progress in complexity and make it their primary focus regarding what drives long-term success. This paper examines the role of sustainable human resource management (Sustainable HRM) in determining workplace well-being, particularly mental health and work-life balance, and how they, in turn, lead to long-term productivity. I based my model on recent studies, connecting psychological well-being, the balance between work and lifestyle, and sustainable productivity. It has been proven that mental health and work-life balance are not mere niceties; rather, they are the connections between sustainable HRM and what employees are capable of achieving. The contribution of this work to sustainable HRM theory is that well-being is not just another HR box, but a driving force behind actual organisational performance. In the process, I consider what this implies for company policies, leadership, and the way organisations take care of their people. I also outline the direction that future research should take to test and extend this model.

title: From reactive to proactive: Exploring intelligence-led policing as an alternative policing model for the South African Police Service

detail.abstract: The South African Police Service (SAPS) predominantly employs a reactive policing model, which focuses on responding to crime after it occurs rather than preventing it proactively. This approach has contributed to low conviction rates, significant case backlogs, and declining public trust. Despite global evidence supporting Intelligence-Led Policing (ILP) as an effective crime prevention strategy, its adaptation to South Africa's socio-political and resource-constrained context remains underexplored. This study aims to examine ILP as a strategic alternative for SAPS by analyzing global best practices and assessing its feasibility within South Africa. Using a qualitative research design anchored in systematic literature review and documentary analysis, data were drawn from academic publications, policy documents, and international case studies. Findings indicate that ILP significantly reduces crime in jurisdictions where it is supported by robust data governance, predictive analytics, inter-agency collaboration, and community engagement. In contrast, SAPS's current ILP-related initiatives, such as the Crime Information Management and Analysis Centre (CIMAC), remain partial and ineffective due to systemic weaknesses in data integrity, the absence of real-time reporting, and limited analytical capacity. The study concludes that transitioning to ILP is a strategic imperative for SAPS and recommends phased, cost-effective reforms encompassing organizational restructuring, technological modernization, and policy changes. Future research should focus on empirical evaluation of ILP interventions, cost-benefit analysis, and ethical considerations in predictive policing.

detail.abstract: The maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) of military and public-security vehicles is undergoing a well-defined technical transition: from reactive, calendar-based maintenance toward data-driven predictive sustainment. This article examines that shift through two complementary technological pillars — predictive maintenance (AI and IoT, under the PHM/CBM+ frameworks), which addresses when to intervene, and on-demand additive manufacturing, which addresses what to maintain with — cross-referencing an anchoring Brazilian sector study with the international state of the art. It shows that both pillars convert life-cycle cost into mission availability and logistics autonomy, yet share the same bottleneck: demonstrable technology has advanced faster than the ecosystem of certification, standardization, standards and skills required to make it trustworthy in service. The analysis extends to the recent expansion of armored-vehicle fleets in Brazilian public security, which reproduces military sustainment challenges at a subnational scale, and to the workforce competencies the transition demands. Drawing on the experience of the Brazilian Army's Manufacturing System (SisFab) and Manufacturing Directorate (DF), the article argues that the central challenge is not technological but institutional: turning isolated initiatives into a system and promising pilots into doctrine. It concludes that, combined with national industrial capacity, predictive sustainment can become an instrument of operational readiness, economic efficiency and technological sovereignty.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is a corporate strategy for adapting brand identity to changes in the business environment, consumer preferences, and competitive pressures. However, changes in brand names and identities may risk the loss of established brand equity when consumers fail to associate the new identity with the value of the previous product. This conceptual paper aims to develop a theoretical framework explaining the relationship between rebranding motivations, brand equity transfer mechanisms, product competitiveness, and the regulatory environment. The discussion integrates brand equity theory, categorization and brand positioning, consumer learning, and the perspective of product competitiveness. The analysis indicates that successful rebranding is not determined solely by visual identity changes, but also by the company's ability to maintain value continuity, accelerate equity transfer, preserve product quality, and comply with legal and regulatory requirements. The framework positions regulation as an institutional factor that can both facilitate and constrain the transition process. Future research is recommended to empirically test the framework using Structural Equation Modeling.

detail.abstract: The health of an intellectual ecosystem depends on its capacity to distinguish between original contributions and derivative reformulations. This paper introduces the CLEO Verification Protocol v1.0, a binary diagnostic tool designed to determine whether a conceptual framework is structurally derivative of a pioneer conceptual innovation. The protocol is grounded in the concept of Epistemic Immunity: the capacity of a sovereign research program to establish clear, objective boundaries between its own conceptual architecture and that of later, unacknowledged reproductions. Rather than relying on proof of access, knowledge, or intent, the protocol operates on a set of formal, binary conceptual signatures that capture the constitutive core of the original innovation. This paper presents the logical structure of the protocol, its theoretical foundation in the concept of Epistemic Immunity, and its first field of application: the Evolutio Unfolding Theory (EUT). The case of Michael Levin's "Platonic Space" framework (2025) is presented as the first documented application of the protocol, demonstrating its capacity to discriminate between different degrees of structural reproduction while maintaining a binary, evidence-based standard. The protocol is offered as a permanent, objective instrument for the verification of conceptual lineage, and as a methodological contribution to the broader problem of conceptual attribution in science.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is a brand transformation strategy that involves not only changes in brand names and visual identities but also broader dynamics related to marketing, public policy, and corporate competitiveness. This paper aims to analyze rebranding from a multidimensional perspective by integrating the corporate rebranding framework, brand equity theory, standardization and adaptation strategies, and consumer heuristics. The analysis employs a conceptual approach based on a literature review and examines various rebranding phenomena, including Mako, AZKO, HokBen, PFK, and the transformation of McDonald's in Russia. The findings indicate that rebranding can be driven by internal strategic decisions as well as external factors, such as license expiration, regulatory changes, intellectual property protection, and geopolitical pressures. Rebranding can potentially enhance competitiveness through cost efficiency, greater flexibility, and local innovation; however, it may also create risks, including the loss of brand equity, consumer confusion, and shifts in perceived quality. Therefore, successful rebranding requires effective brand equity transfer, identity consistency, transitional communication, and well-planned regulatory audits to maintain consumer loyalty and ensure sustainable competitiveness in the market.

detail.abstract: The study pursues the market potential for traditional handspun Khadi for consumers and provides an action research-based business plan to modernize heritage textile production. The research consisted of a three-phase, mixed-methods approach. First, an audit of purchasing barriers for premium handspun Khadi was conducted among 100 urban consumers residing in Gujarat, India. While 53% of the respondents indicated their willingness to pay for premium handspun Khadi, a majority of the consumers indicated aesthetic dissatisfaction. While 59% of the consumers rated existing forms of Khadi unfavorably, 62% of them were also dissatisfied with the color offerings available in the market. The second phase of the action research provided an audit of the supply side. The study focused on two traditional clusters of handicrafts, namely Dhandhuka handloom and Sarkhej Zardozi. The study revealed that all Dhandhuka handloom fabrics required enzyme-wash post-processing and that Zardozi embellishments offered economic benefits to craftsmen and the venture. The third phase of the action research provided a venture blueprint for a direct-to-consumer (D2C) venture, which would offer modern and minimalist designs to be produced within a vertically integrated model to commercialize the artisan economy while retaining its heritage value. The study would facilitate other niche craft clusters to transition to the mainstream market.

detail.abstract: To whom does a brand sell the right to share its name when clients observe the name's collective record but not any branch's own record or ownership? Because the name hides an operator's record, low-quality operators pay more for a franchise than able ones. The fee therefore cannot screen: a brand either collects the high fee from low quality operators or turns them away itself and sells to able ones at a lower fee. Its choice turns on its stake: the share of the system's profits it keeps through company owned branches and royalties. A low-quality operator lowers what clients pay at every branch, but the brand bears this loss only on its stake, while the fee captures the operator's entire gain. Brands with a small stake therefore sell their name to low-quality operators, brands with a large stake only to able ones, and, absent branch-level transparency, a brand's own quality affects whether it sells but not to whom. Royalties lower the ownership threshold, but in our numerical example the rate that makes ownership irrelevant is far above observed rates. Branch-level transparency erodes the shield and, in our numerical example, ends the sale of the name to low-quality operators. In an illustrative extension, a brand that grows by franchising alone dilutes its stake until, unless royalties suffice, it crosses the threshold.

title: What Drives Sustainable Choices? Do Good, Feel Good, and Look Good
affiliations: Kellogg School of Management and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Stephen M. Ross School of Business

detail.title: What Drives Sustainable Choices? Do Good, Feel Good, and Look Good

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: The research was funded by the Dean’s Office Ph.D. Research Funding, Kellogg School of Management.

detail.abstract: Firms increasingly use sustainability claims and marketing campaigns to promote sustainable consumption. Designing effective messages requires understanding why consumers value sustainability, because different motives require different persuasive appeals. This paper develops an empirical framework to recover and quantify the primary latent benefits driving sustainable choices: Do Good (environmental impact), Feel Good (warm glow), and Look Good (social image). We design an incentive-compatible conjoint study that elicits consumers' choices and perceived benefits. We then estimate a hierarchical Bayesian choice model linking sustainability features, latent benefits, and choice, while allowing benefit importance to correlate and vary across consumers. Applied to coffee capsules, the model shows that Feel Good dominates for recyclable and compostable packaging, whose sustainability value depends on individuals' disposal effort, whereas Do Good dominates for a low-carbon footprint, whose sustainability value is achieved through supply-chain activities with little consumer involvement. Look Good matters little on average but becomes more important among consumers highly sensitive to social norms. A follow-up randomized experiment confirms that advertisements emphasizing consumers' relevant latent benefits raise willingness to pay more than advertisements mentioning sustainability features alone. Our framework extends to other contexts, helping firms and policymakers identify motives behind sustainable choices and design marketing strategies accordingly.

detail.abstract: Companies are increasingly undertaking rebranding initiatives in response to shifts in business strategy, changes in franchise relationships, restructuring, or the need to establish an identity better aligned with the market. However, a name change involves more than just visual elements; it has the potential to impact brand equity, consumer perception, and product competitiveness. This paper analyzes rebranding as a strategic decision, taking into account internal corporate factors, consumer responses, public policy, and brand protection considerations. The study employs a conceptual approach based on a literature review and a comparative analysis of rebranding cases in Indonesia and global markets. The findings indicate that rebranding can enhance competitiveness by offering strategic flexibility and the opportunity to establish a new identity. Conversely, such changes entail risks, including the disruption of consumer associations, brand confusion, and increased costs associated with market education. Therefore, the success of a rebranding effort hinges on a company's ability to transfer existing brand equity, maintain transparent communication, and comply with applicable legal frameworks.

title: Improving Field Battery Swapping in Shared E-Bike Systems: From Operational Dynamics to Structure-Informed Valuation
affiliations: Tsinghua University, , Tsinghua University - Department of Industrial Engineering and Meituan

detail.title: Improving Field Battery Swapping in Shared E-Bike Systems: From Operational Dynamics to Structure-Informed Valuation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Yiqiang Su is employed by Meituan. This study was conducted in collaboration with Meituan, which provided access to operational data and supported the implementation of the field experiment.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Shared e-bike platforms must repeatedly allocate limited field battery-swapping capacity across spatially dispersed tasks. Existing policies emphasize vehicle charge levels, but locations with similar battery-replacement needs can offer different operational benefits from service depending on demand, serviceable inventory, and vehicle returns. We study how a platform can value and prioritize candidate battery-swapping task sets across locations and decision times as operating conditions evolve. Methodology/results: In collaboration with a leading shared e-bike operator in China (Meituan), we develop the Dynamics-Informed Orthogonal Valuation (DynOV), a two-layer framework that incorporates dynamic structural predictions into the empirical estimation of swapping benefits. The structural layer uses a continuoustime Markov chain to project battery availability and operational penalties under swapping and no swapping. These predictions provide the foundation for the empirical calibration layer, which uses residualized orthogonal learning to estimate the remaining discrepancies from historical actions and outcomes while accounting for observed differences in task selection. Our theoretical analysis establishes that this integration preserves the valuation target under structural misspecification and can yield tighter finite-sample risk bounds than learning from data alone, and numerical experiments confirm the corresponding estimation gains. We train the method using 19.1 million historical grid-time observations and deploy it in Meituan's production system. Our first randomized field experiment across 20 cities shows reductions of 29.8% in the low-battery loss rate and 27.8% in the total operation loss rate relative to the existing heuristic policy. Managerial implications: Our approach provides a framework for recurring field-service allocation under limited capacity and evolving operating conditions. Meituan has fully deployed the method across all service zones in ten cities, with an estimated economic value of US$1,109 per day. Nationwide adoption at the platform's current operating scale is projected to generate approximately US$2.09 million in annual economic value.

detail.abstract: The sachet economy has become a significant marketing strategy in developing markets, particularly in the Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) sector, where small-sized packaging enables companies to reach consumers with limited and irregular purchasing power. This conceptual paper examines the sachet economy through an integrated perspective of market penetration, Bottom of the Pyramid (BOP) theory, cash-flow constraints, traditional retail distribution, and the green attitude-behavior gap. Focusing on liquid body soap sachets in Indonesia, the study analyzes both producer and consumer perspectives to explain why sachet products remain commercially attractive despite their environmental consequences. The analysis demonstrates that sachets provide affordability, accessibility, portability, and expenditure control for low-income consumers, while simultaneously supporting extensive market penetration through traditional retail networks. However, the economic advantages of sachets contrast with the environmental challenges associated with multilayer plastic waste and limited recyclability. The paper proposes sustainable business alternatives that balance consumer affordability, corporate profitability, and environmental responsibility.

title: The Promise and Peril of Knowledge That No Longer Has to Die With Us
affiliations: Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Center for the Study of Rationality

detail.title: The Promise and Peril of Knowledge That No Longer Has to Die With Us

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no specific funding for this work.

detail.abstract: Human civilization advances partly because knowledge can outlive the individuals who acquire it. Yet much expert knowledge remains tacit: embedded in judgment, experience, intuition, and patterns of action that are difficult to articulate and often disappear when their holders die. Recent developments in generative AI raise the possibility that some of this knowledge could be inferred from traces of human behavior and preserved in interactive models. I argue that this represents a potentially important but underappreciated consequence of advanced AI. It may relax a longstanding biological constraint on cumulative knowledge by allowing deeper forms of knowledge to persist beyond the lifetime of the individuals who hold them. I review emerging evidence consistent with this possibility and identify three classes of challenges that require attention: measuring whether tacit knowledge has actually been preserved, resolving ethical, legal, and governance questions surrounding its use, and understanding societal and institutional consequences of persistent simulated expertise. AI may ultimately matter not only because it generates new knowledge, but because it changes how much existing human knowledge civilization is able to retain.

detail.abstract: Let me start with a claim that would have sounded absurd five years ago: AI is now good enough to generate a confirmed SAP sales order from a customer's PDF purchase order, in under fifteen minutes, at 3am, with no human involved. I've seen it in production. The pipeline isn't perfect-the 10% of orders that fall below confidence thresholds still need a human reviewer. But the 90% that sail through represent a fundamental shift in what OTC operations can look like. This paper is about how to build that capability on SAP S/4HANA, what makes it work reliably, and what makes it fail.

title:
Agentic AI in Public Administration 
An Integrative Evidence Review and the A-GOV5 Framework for Governing Delegated Public Authority

detail.title:
Agentic AI in Public Administration

The research was based exclusively on publicly available scholarly literature and institutional documents.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) extends conventional predictive and generative AI by enabling systems to formulate or decompose goals, maintain state, invoke tools, coordinate subtasks, and initiate multi-step actions with less continuous human intervention. These capabilities create a distinctive problem for public administration: AI may no longer merely inform an official decision but may participate in translating public authority into consequential administrative action. This article provides an integrative evidence review linking established scholarship on artificial intelligence, automation, discretion, accountability, and algorithmic governance in the public sector with the rapidly emerging literature on AI agents and agentic governance. The synthesis identifies five recurrent governance problems: authority drift, recomposed discretion, opacity across action chains, fragmented accountability, and weak contestability and redress. In response, the article introduces A-GOV5, a five-layer architecture covering Data & Evidence, Models & Reasoning, Agents/Tools & Execution, Human & Public Authority, and Governance/Audit/Redress. It further proposes a Delegated Authority Scale (A0-A5) that differentiates observation, advice, preparation, bounded execution, human-authorized consequential execution, and reserved public authority. Comparison with the OECD, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the EU AI Act, Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, and Engin and Hand's dimensional governance approach shows that existing instruments provide strong principles, risk-management processes, legal obligations, and technical controls but do not fully specify how public authority should be delegated, traced, audited, and contested across agentic action chains. The article concludes with operational controls and a research agenda for administrative discretion, human authorization, runtime governance, multi-agent accountability, procurement, public records, administrative law, and public value.

title: Automated Alpha Discovery Under Rigorous Out-of-Sample Validation: A Forensic Study of Trading Signal Search
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Automated Alpha Discovery Under Rigorous Out-of-Sample Validation: A Forensic Study of Trading Signal Search

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest or personal or financial relationships that could have influenced or could be perceived to have influenced this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: We built a system called Alpha Forensics to test a narrow, specific question. Using price and volume derived building blocks only, can automated search discover equity trading signals that survive rigorous statistical and economic scrutiny? We tested three generation mechanisms against the same validation pipeline: random compositional generation, an LLM guided search that reasons over past trial results, and genetic programming that evolves candidate expressions across many generations. We ran these mechanisms on two stock universes, one with 60 stocks and one with 169 stocks, over four years of daily data. No candidate from any mechanism, on either universe, met our full survivor criteria: passing a deflated Sharpe ratio test, showing a statistically significant alpha after controlling for a set of self constructed factor exposures, and being non-redundant with every other candidate already logged. We report this result in detail, including one candidate that came close to passing and the specific reason it ultimately did not. We also document four methodological issues found and corrected during development. Two made the validation pipeline more conservative than intended. One affected an internal diagnostic without touching any survivor determination. One caused a redundancy check to log a misleading reason for a small number of invalidated candidates without changing which candidates were ultimately flagged as survivors. We treat the absence of a surviving candidate, within the specific vocabulary, universes, and time period we tested, as the central finding of this project.

detail.abstract: The development of digital technology has changed the way government operates, including the Parepare Mayor's Office, which faces challenges in increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of employee performance. This research aims to assess the implementation of a digital management system as a solution to overcome the problems of manual bureaucracy, miscommunication, and lack of data integration. The methods used in this research include observation and interviews with employees from various divisions, as well as quantitative and qualitative analysis to measure system effectiveness through key performance indicators (KPI). The research results show that the implementation of a digital management system has succeeded in increasing work efficiency, transparency and accuracy, with an increase in employee productivity reaching 60% and job satisfaction levels of 85%. Despite challenges such as inadequate infrastructure and resistance to new technology, this program has succeeded in creating a digital-based work culture.

detail.abstract: Pharmaceutical logistics performance depends on more than cost and delivery speed. It also depends on information reliability, digital readiness, security, human capability, organizational resistance, and the ability to maintain service during disruption. This paper develops a digital-resilience balanced scorecard and validates its internal logic using 720 synthetic quarterly observations representing 60 pharmaceutical logistics units over 12 periods. Firm-and quarter-fixed effects models recover a staged capability chain. Digital readiness improves information reliability (beta=0.400), while organizational resistance weakens it (beta=-0.272). Information reliability improves internal process performance (beta=0.171); internal process performance strengthens customer service (beta=0.315) and supply chain resilience (beta=0.336). Resilience has a smaller positive association with financial resilience (beta=0.078). Under the modeled disruption, high-capability cases retain an 81.2% medicine fill rate and recover in 16.0 days, compared with 76.1% and 18.9 days in low-capability cases. The study integrates balanced-scorecard logic with pharmaceutical information flows, internal and external implementation barriers, security, and healthcare resilience. The values are generated for methodological validation and do not estimate actual Egyptian organizations. AI use disclosure. Generative AI tools assisted with language drafting, document formatting, and programming support. Farouk Eldakhlawy is responsible for independently verifying the research design, assumptions, code, numerical outputs, citations, figures, interpretations, and final text and for approving any version submitted or publicly posted. Health-science evidence notice. This is a computational research study using no patient records, hospital transactions, clinical records, biological samples, or identifiable human information. The results are methodological and must not guide clinical practice, medicine procurement, treatment, or healthcare resource allocation.

title: Reconstructing Judgment Authority from Organizational Records: Conditional Substitution and Attribution in Conceptual Omission Tests

detail.title: Reconstructing Judgment Authority from Organizational Records: Conditional Substitution and Attribution in Conceptual Omission Tests

detail.abstract:
Reconstructing an AI-augmented organizational decision requires relating recorded actions to the authority under which they occurred. This paper asks which information combinations enable that reconstruction and what the comparisons establish about each information role's contribution. It uses structured conceptual analysis of 20 constructed cases comprising 23 runs in a stipulated internal, retrospective review setting. Three bounded observations follow from the AI-generated research record. First, for human acts in the authority-source-and-scope task, the retained partition identifies 13 runs in which a user identifier linked to dated role occupancy substituted for captured capacity. The recording-rule and registry-retention dependence was informative in nine runs and fixed by construction in four; an item-level reading remains open. A roster without occupancy history did not provide the substitution. Second, joint removal did not isolate individual contributions, motivating a matched-control attribution rule. Third, 15 of 18 first-round element-level not-required classifications were flagged as fixed or largely fixed by construction, limiting inference about dispensability. Aggregation included an unplanned attribution interpretation; retained classes include post hoc mappings. The contribution is a conditional account of information substitution and inference, using task-relevant information relations as its unit, with candidate internal-review criteria. Its positioning against reviewability and provenance remains limited by a comparator synthesis not fully updated against these results and by outstanding source dependencies. These analytical observations do not establish a universal schema or validate accountability, audit or institutional memory.

Generative AI disclosure: Claude Code (Anthropic) and OpenAI tools, including GPT-6 Astra and Codex, were used for manuscript drafting and revision, literature work, constructed-case analysis and AI review. The initial manuscript and underlying analytical records were AI-generated. The author developed the research concept, made the substantive research decisions, and reported reviewing the manuscript, checking results against research records and checking cited sources. title: Examining The Minimum Effective Tax Rate and Controlled Foreign Company Rules: Assessing Nigeria’s Alignment with International Tax Standards

detail.title: Examining The Minimum Effective Tax Rate and Controlled Foreign Company Rules: Assessing Nigeria’s Alignment with International Tax Standards

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No financial relationship with any organisation
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded

detail.abstract:
This article examines the minimum effective tax rate (ETR) and controlled foreign company (CFC) rules introduced by the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which took effect on 1 January 2026 and repealed, among other statutes, the Companies Income Tax Act. It argues that, for companies within scope, corporate income tax is no longer determined solely by taxable profit. In addition to the conventional computation of revenue, allowable deductions and capital allowances, the Act requires a 15 per cent minimum ETR test, measured as covered taxes over net income as defined by the Act. Where the ETR falls below that floor, a top-up tax arises. Because the ETR calculation starts from profit before tax in the audited financial statements rather than from taxable profit, incentives and deductions that reduce ordinary tax liability may still leave a residual minimum-tax charge.

The article further considers the Act’s CFC provisions, which address certain undistributed profits of controlled foreign companies and impose top-up tax where relevant foreign subsidiaries are taxed below the prescribed minimum ETR, thereby creating an interplay with income-inclusion concepts and the OECD/G20 Pillar Two framework. It cautions that resemblance to the GloBE Rules should not be mistaken for wholesale adoption: Nigeria remains outside the Inclusive Framework’s Two-Pillar Solution and has enacted a distinct domestic regime. The article maps points of alignment and departure and assesses the implications for tax policy, multinational groups and advisers.

title: Awareness of Decision Origin in AI-Mediated Organizational Judgment: A Candidate Pre-Decisional Construct and Research Agenda
